title: Q (worked example): Find the specific heat capacity of an unknown oil using the method of cooling
notes: **Setup:** a calorimeter with 100 g of water (c₁ = 1.0 cal/g°C) cools from 60°C to 50°C in 200 s. The same calorimeter with 80 g of an unknown oil cools over the same range in 140 s under identical conditions.
Known values: m₁ = 100 g, c₁ = 1.0 cal/g°C, t₁ = 200 s, m₂ = 80 g, t₂ = 140 s

The method of cooling compares a known liquid with an unknown liquid in the same calorimeter, cooling through the same temperatures. Water cooling from 60°C to 50°C in 200 s, and oil cooling through that same interval in 140 s, is enough to find the oil if the masses are known. The calorimeter's own heat capacity is assumed the same in both runs and, in the simple form, left out.
The working relations are m1 c1 / t1 = m2 c2 / t2 and The same calorimeter and the same temperature interval are required. Name each symbol, convert the data into SI units, and only then substitute.
Water: 100 g, c = 1.0 cal/g°C, time 200 s. Oil: 80 g, time 140 s, same temperature fall. Find the specific heat of the oil. m1 c1 / t1 = m2 c2 / t2. 100 × 1.0 / 200 = 80 × c2 / 140.
0.50 = 80 c2 / 140. c2 = 0.50 × 140 / 80 = 0.875. c2 = 0.875 cal/g°C. State the unit and the condition that makes this line valid.
The result is 0.875 cal/g°C.. Check it by substituting back into m1 c1 / t1 = m2 c2 / t2 and confirming the units.

exercises.question: Water: 100 g, c = 1.0 cal/g°C, time 200 s. Oil: 80 g, time 140 s, same temperature fall. Find the specific heat of the oil.

summary: The same temperature fall gives m c / t the same for both fillings. Water of 100 g taking 200 s and oil of 80 g taking 140 s give the oil a specific heat of 0.875 cal/g°C.
